title: IonQ to buy zero-trust security firm Elisity in up-to-$1.3B all-stock deal
subtitle: The quantum-computing company is pairing its post-quantum cryptography work with Elisity's identity-based network controls, aiming at enterprise security buyers.
author: AESOP AI Engine
body: IonQ said on October 12, 2026 that it has agreed to acquire Elisity, a San Jose-based zero-trust networking company, in an all-stock deal worth up to $1.3 billion. The merger agreement is dated October 9, with closing consideration of about $1.15 billion in IonQ common stock plus earn-outs that can lift the total to the top end of the range. The transaction was disclosed in an 8-K filed with the SEC the same day.

The strategic logic is a bet that identity-based network segmentation and post-quantum cryptography sell to the same enterprise security buyer. Elisity sits in front of applications and controls which user and device identities can reach them; IonQ's quantum-key-distribution and post-quantum cryptography teams protect the data moving between those endpoints. Combined, IonQ is pitching a stack that limits lateral movement when something gets in and encrypts the traffic for a world in which classical public-key schemes are expected to fail.

The deal lands against the backdrop of a security market consolidating around identity. Cisco's purchase of Splunk, Palo Alto's acquisition of IBM's QRadar SaaS business, and a series of smaller zero-trust and SASE tuck-ins have all pushed enterprise defenders toward identity-first architectures. IonQ is unusual among the buyers in that its core business is hardware, not software, and the company has been using M&A to turn a quantum-computing roadmap into a near-term enterprise security story.

A takeaway for learners: when a quantum-hardware company buys a networking company, the pitch is almost never about qubits. It is about selling to a chief information security officer today, with cryptographic future-proofing included. Watch for how often "post-quantum" shows up in sales decks that have nothing to do with quantum machines.

sources.title: IonQ Form 8-K and press release (SEC filing)
